items.headline: Procter & Gamble plans to run more factories without on‑site workers to cut costs
items.summary: The consumer‑goods giant will expand unattended shift capability at 15 sites and aims to add more by 2027, part of a broader automation push to reduce labor expenses. The move raises questions about job security in manufacturing while promising lower production costs for the company.
